findings.title: Harvest fails for an exited run whose `review.ndjson` is missing. Handle the absent stream in `completeLocalReview`.

findings.body:
**Re-check that fetched commits exist before resolving their trees.**

`ensureObjects` runs `git fetch --prune --quiet origin` when `base` or `head` is missing, then returns without checking again. If a commit is still absent after the fetch, `resolveFacts` fails on `git rev-parse <commit>^{tree}` (line 30, called at lines 36 and 38). The error is a generic `GitUnavailable` with git's stderr, and it is raised before identity resolution runs. Verify both commits after the fetch. If either is still missing, throw an error that names the missing commit so the failure is specific.
findings.title: Re-check that fetched commits exist before resolving their trees.

findings.body:
**Bound the `paseo send` call with a termination signal that cannot be handled.**

`spawnNotifySend` calls `spawnSync` with `timeout` but no `killSignal` (`src/adapters/crq/notifySource.ts:48-51`). When the deadline passes, Node sends the default `SIGTERM`. If the child handles `SIGTERM` and does not exit, `spawnSync` keeps waiting. The call also blocks the event loop, so no async watchdog can interrupt it. The documented 30 s and 90 s deadlines (`src/adapters/crq/notifySource.ts:5`, `:29-31`) are then not enforced. Publication can stall for as long as the child stays alive.

Add `killSignal: 'SIGKILL'` so the timeout always terminates the child. Other bounded `spawnSync` calls in this repository already use this pattern (for example `src/adapters/crq/publishSource.ts:123`, `src/adapters/crq/summarySource.ts:86`).

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
   const result = spawnSync('paseo', argv, {
     encoding: 'utf8',
     timeout: hasHost ? HOST_TIMEOUT_MS : LOCAL_TIMEOUT_MS,
+    killSignal: 'SIGKILL',
   });
```

</details>
findings.title: Bound the `paseo send` call with a termination signal that cannot be handled.
